ὅ.definition: relat. Pron. masc. for v. c; neut. of relat. Pron

ὅ γε.definition: the demonstr. Pron. made; Il.13.94; 7.169; . . there he sitteth, 19.344; with a Subst., he the hero, 5.327; ib.794

ὄα.definition: service-tree, Sorbus domestica, Thphr; its fruit was sorbapple, or service- berry, which was split and pickled for use, Pl.Smp.190d, Dsc.1.120:—in Pl.l.c. codd. have and in Dsc. which latter form also occurs in Hp.Vic…

ὀβολός.definition: obol, used both as a weight and coin, at; as a weight, Gal.13.295, etc. , cf. Plu.Lys.17.)

ὄγκιον.definition: or case or casket for arrows and other implements, Od.21.61, cf. Hermipp.16

ὄγκος.definition: barb of an arrow, in pl., the barbed; brackets, Moschio ap.Ath.5.208b

ὄγμος.definition: furrow in ploughing; swathe in reaping, Il.11.68; . . 18.552, cf. 557; Theoc.10.2

ὀδούς.definition: nom. Arist.EN1161b23, LXX1; metaph., Luc.Am.3; the tooth of grief, Ach.Tat. l.c

ὀθόννα.definition: greater celandine, Chelidonium majus; juice of I, Dsc.2.182; also, the juice of various other plants, ibid., cf. Zopyr. ap. Orib.14.45.4

ὄθριξ.definition: gen. poet. for with like hair, Il.2.765, prob. l. for Sophr.52

οἴαξ.definition: Ion. prop. handle of; in Il.24.269, are prob. rings of the yoke, through which pass the reins for guiding the mules, cf

οἶβος.definition: piece of meat from the back of an ox's neck, Luc.Lex.3

οἶδμα.definition: swelling, swell, in Hom. only of; the swelling of the south-west wind, AP9.36

οἶδος.definition: swelling, tumour, produced by internal action, Hp.Fract.25 , VC17 , Nic.Th.188, 237, 426; puffiness, Aret.SD1.16

οἰκεῖος.definition: also E.Heracl.634; Ion; Astrol., domiciliary signs, Vett.Val.37.21, al

οἶκος.definition: house, not only of built houses, but of any; freq. omitted after or v. I.4c, A.I.2

οἶμα.definition: spring, rush, swoop, Il.16.752; 21.252; of a serpent, Q.S.6.201, etc

οἴνη.definition: old name for the vine; = wine, AP6.334 , Nic.Th.622

οἶνος.definition: fermented juice of other kinds, barley wine, a kind of beer, Hdt.2.77; palm-wine, ib.86, cf. 1.193; lotus- wine, Id.4.177, etc.; from which drinks grape-wine is expressly distd., Id.2.60

οἰνοῦττα.definition: cake or porridge of barley mixed; a plant with intoxicating properties, Arist.Fr.107

ὄϊος.definition: of a sheep, ewe-milk, Hp.Vict.2.41; Polem.Hist.88; more sheepish than a sheep, Sophr.122 . shd. be read ; cf

ὀϊστός.definition: a plant, arrow-head, Sagitta sagittifolia, Mago ap.Plin.HN21.111

οἶστρος.definition: gadfly, breese, prob. Tabanus bovinus, an; an insect that infests tunny-fish, prob. Brachiella thynni, ib.557a27,602a28

οἴσυον.definition: wickerwork, dub.l.in Aen.Tact.29.11; in the basket-market, Lycurg.112

οἰωνός.definition: a large bird, bird of prey; generally, birds, opp. beasts, S.Fr.941.11; so in

ὄκρις.definition: jagged point or prominence, any; as Adj. = rugged, A.Pr.1016. 'arx, mons', OLat. ocris = mons confragosus.)

ὀκτάς.definition: the number eight, Arist.Metaph.1082a30; body of eight men, Nic.Dam.60 J

ὀκτήρης.definition: warship with eight rowers to each oar, Plb.16.3.2, Plu.Ant.61

ὀλβιστήρ.definition: one who makes prosperous, Dioscorus in PLit.Lond.981i7

ὄλονθος.definition: edible fruit of the wild; sterile summer fruit of the cultivated fig, Gal.12.133

ὀλοόφρων.definition: meaning mischief; in Od., crafty, sagacious, of persons, 1.52; 10.137; 11.322

ὀλός.definition: = the ink of the cuttle-fish; metaph., blood, AP15.25.1

ὅλος.definition: Ion. as in Hom. (twice, v; whole, i. e. safe and sound, Lys.6.12, cf. Pl.Men.77a

ὄλπη.definition: leathern oil-flask, esp. used in the

ὁμάς.definition: the whole, all together, Gp.10.2.3; in one lump sum, Men.Prot.p.15 D.; but comprehensively, Just.Edict.13Praef

ὁμηγερής.definition: assembled, . . Il.15.84; they were all assembled, 1.57, al.; cf

ὅμορος.definition: Ep. and Ion. having the same; metaph., bordering on, closely resembling, Arist.EE1232a25; Plot.4.8.7

ὀναγός.definition: dialect form of Att. ass-driver, v.l. in Plaut. Asin.Prolog.10; cf. I

ὄνειρος.definition: or the masc. form freq. in; in similes or metaphors, of anything unreal or fleeting, Od.11.207, cf. 222; if only in a dream, 19.581; faint and shadowy traces, Pl.Lg.695c; dreams of wealth, APl.c

ὀνήμων.definition: gen. = of Hermes and Aphrodite, Cat.Cod. Astr.2.203

ὀνίας.definition: a sea-fish, a kind of scarus, perh. Smaris vulgaris, Nic. Thyat. ap. Ath.7.320c

ὄνιννος.definition: parasite found in sea-weed, perh. millepede, Thphr.HP4.6.8 codd

ὄνυξ.definition: Hom. only in Ep. dat. pl. and; warmed me to my fingers' ends, ib.159; so AP9.709 , cf. 12.93 ; so also from the fingers' ends, ib.5.13 , Plu.2.3c; but from childhood, Horace's de tenero ungui, AP5.128

ὄνωνις.definition: or rest-harrow, Ononis antiquorum, Thphr.HP6.1.3, Dsc.3.131; Call.Fr.anon.366 : metaph., this troublesome weed , Com.Adesp.438

ὀξύς.definition: wood sorrel, Oxalis Acetosella; = great sea-rush, Juncus acutus, ib.21.113

ὀξυσιτία.definition: a disorder in which the food turns acid on the stomach, like Aristid.Or.47.9

ὀξύτης.definition: sharpness, pointedness, of acute; of sound, sharpness, opp. Id.Phlb.17c, Tht.163c

ὄον.definition: the fruit of the service-tree, v

ὀπή.definition: hole in the roof, serving as a chimney, = Ar.V.317 , 350; Id.Fr.11, cf. Xenarch.4.11

ὀπίας.definition: cheese made from milk curdled with fig-juice , Ar.V.353 ; in full, E.Cyc.136, cf. Ath.14.658c; v

ὀπιτίων.definition: tuberous root of Bunium ferulaceum, earth-nut, Thphr.HP7.13.9

ὅπλον.definition: tool, implement, mostly in pl., like; a ship's tackle, tackling, Hom. , 2.390, al., Hes.Op.627; esp. ropes, halyards, etc., Od.2.430, etc.; in which sense Hom. twice uses the sg., rope, 14.346, 21.390: generally, any …

ὁποῖος.definition: Ep. Hom., but twice; as Relat., of what sort or quality, as [is] the word thou hast spoken, such shalt thou hear again, Il.20.250; such as he might be, Od.17.421; S.OT1272

ὀπός.definition: juice, distd. from in that; metaph., the juicy freshness of youth, opp. AP5.257

ὁραῖος.definition: of a boundary: = gruma, Gloss.; cf

ὀργή.definition: natural impulse or propensity; c. gen., visitations of Pan's wrath, Id.Med.1172; but

ὀρειάλωτος.definition: wandering on the mountains, condemned by Thom.Mag.p.267 R

ὄρειον.definition: = mare's tail, Hippuris vulgaris, Plin. HN27.115

ὁρίζων.definition: separating circle (cf; Pythag. name for 9, because it limits, i.e. finishes, the series of units, Theol.Ar.57

ὅριος.definition: of boundaries, guardian of; = Lat. Terminus, D.H.2.74, Plu.Num.16

ὄρκυς.definition: acc. a large kind of tunny, Anaxandr.41.62, Archestr.Fr.34.3, Arist.HA543b5, etc.; cf

ὅρμος.definition: cord, chain, esp. necklace, collar; generally, anything strung like a necklace, wreath, chaplet, Pi.O.2.74; a string of crowns, i. e. of praises, Id.N.4.17

ὄροβος.definition: bitter vetch, Vicia Ervilia, Thphr.HP2.4.2; = II, Eust.853.55

ὁρογενής.definition: productive of terms , Iamb.in Nic.p.57 P

ὀροκάρυον.definition: mountain-nut, a tree which grows near the Black Sea, Str.12.3.12

ὀρός.definition: the watery or serous part of milk, whey; the watery part or serum of the blood, Pl.Ti.83d

ὀροφή.definition: roof of a house, or ceiling of a; top of a beehive, Arist.HA624a6

ὄρρος.definition: end of the os sacrum; generally, rump, Ar.Ra.222, Pax1239, Lys.964, etc. , cf. OE. ears, OHG. ars, etc.: akin also to

ὀρσοδάκνη.definition: an insect which eats the buds of plants, perh. Haltica oleracea, Arist.HA552a30

ὄρυς.definition: a wild animal in Libya, prob. = II.1, Hdt.4.192

ὄρχις.definition: and Att. nom. pl. Ion; in females, ovaries, Gal.2.810, al

ὁσάγωνος.definition: of whatever number of sides, Theo Sm.p.40 H

ὅσος.definition: Ep. both forms in Hom. and Hes; with a partit. gen. in the principal clause, Il.12.13; 5.267; A.Pers.441; . . of all the Achaeans, Il.9.55; which are and which are not . . , Pl.R.467d; on v. A.III

ὄσσα.definition: Att. a rumour, which, from its origin; generally, voice, of the Muses, Hes.Th.10,43,65; of a bull, ib.832

ὀστέον.definition: Att. contr. poet. AP7.480; metaph., i.e. rocks, Choeril.Trag.2

ὄστλιγξ.definition: hair, esp. curled hair, lock of; anything curled or twisted, as

ὀστρύα.definition: and hop hornbeam, Ostrya carpinifolia, Thphr.HP3.10.3, cf. 3.3.1, 3.6.1, Plin.HN13.117; also Thphr.HP1.8.2

ὀσφυήξ.definition: having dislocated one's hip, Poet. ap. Lex. de Spir.p.209 V

ὄσχιον.definition: raised margin of the womb, Gal.19.127; cf

ὄσχις.definition: said to be = Hp.Coac.528; but as the reference is to a male in Id.Epid.7.33 Littré's cj. should be accepted in both places, as also for in ib.5.61

ὄτλος.definition: suffering, distress, arising from a thing, A.Th.18; S.Tr.7

ὀττεία.definition: divination from ominous sounds, D.H.8.37; Id.9.45; evil foreboding, Id.1.38

οὖδας.definition: gen. dat. Il.5.734, al. (more; floor, pavement in rooms and houses, Od.23.46; on the floor of Zeus' abode, Il.24.527; 5.734, 8.385: prov., to bring a man to the pavement, i.e. to strip him of all he has, h.Merc.284

οὐένετος.definition: Lat. venetus, of the faction of the Blues in the chariot races, Tab. Defix.Aud.234.5 :—also ib.237.6; cf. D.C.61.6, 77.10

οὖλος.definition: old Ep. and Ion. form of whole, entire, v; woolly, of thick, fleecy wool

οὐλοφυής.definition: rough, raw, undifferentiated, of lumps of earth , Emp.62.4

οὐρά.definition: Ion. tail, of a lion; = S.Fr.1078, f.l. in Hom.Epigr.12

οὐρανός.definition: Dor. and Boeot. Alcm.23.16; heaven: in Hom. and Hes

οὐραχός.definition: urachus, a foetal organ connected with the; apex of the heart, Hp.Cord.4, cf. Aret.SA1.8

οὖρον.definition: urine, Hdt.2.111, etc.: pl., Hp.Aph.4.69,72, Thphr.Od.60; limit, range, Il.23.431, cf. the range of mules, i.e. the breadth of land ploughed in a day by mules, the length of the furrow being fixed, 10.351: so in sg., …

οὔσκη.definition: glossed in margin by Zos.Alch.p.222 B

οὖσον.definition: ship's tackle, ropes, Lyc.20 , Alex.Aet.3.21, pl. prob. in Antim. Col.6

ὀφιοῦχος.definition: the constellation Ophiuchus; a who interferes with alchemists, Olymp.Alch.p.86 B

ὀφίτης.definition: of or like a serpent; = shingles, Gal.19.440

ὀφίων.definition: mousmon, the wild sheep of Sardinia, Plin.HN28.151, 30.146

ὀφρῦς.definition: acc. in late Poets; alone, scorn, pride, AP7.409 , 9.43 , 10.122 , etc

ὀχεύς.definition: Ep. anything used for holding; band or strap for fastening the helmet under the chin, Il.3.372

ὄχθη.definition: older form of any height or rising ground, natural or artificial, bank, dyke by the side of a river, Il.21.171, cf. 172: in sg., also, Plu.Publ.16, Arr.An.1.14.4, CPHerm. 95.10 : mostly in pl., raised banks of a river…

ὄχθοιβος.definition: purple stripe down the front of the; neckband, IG12.387.35, cf. 22.1388.84, 1400.67; ib.1425.309

ὄχθος.definition: eminence, bank, hill, first in h.Ap.17; tubercle in leprosy, Aret.SD2.13, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.28.3

ὄχος.definition: carriage, used by Hom. in heterocl; the swift or round bearers of the chariot, i.e. the wheels, E.IA146

ὄψ.definition: poetic Noun, used in obliq. cases of sg; gen. = the eye, face, Emp.88, Antim.63

ὀψαμάτης.definition: Dor. for one who mows till late at even, Theoc.10.7

ὀψίνοος.definition: late-observing, i.e. remiss, inobservant, of Epimetheus, Pi.P.5.28

ὀψιπέδων.definition: one who has long been in fetters, Men.1049

ὀαρίζω.definition: Ep. Verb, used only in pres. and impf., converse or chat with , c. dat. pers., Il.6.516; 22.127; h.Merc.170: c.acc. cogn., h.Hom.23.3: contr. impf., h.Merc.58

ὀαριστύς.definition: Ep., = familiar converse; as concrete, the company of out- fighters, 13.291

ὀβελεία.definition: an unknown iron object, in pl., IG22.1631.409, 1672.310: sg., in a list of cups, etc., prob. in ib. 1695.14, 15

ὀβελία.definition: perh. a tax of an obol, SIG1000.3

ὀβελίζω.definition: mark with a critical obelus , Cic.Fam.9.10.1, Hermog.Id.2.3:—Pass., ibid

ὁδεύω.definition: c. acc. loci, travel over, A.R.4.1441; Plu.Eum.15; IG 14.2012A36; . . Epigr.Gr.226.3 :— Pass., thoroughfare, highway, POxy. 1537.18 , Stud.Pal.20.117.6

ὅδισμα.definition: a way compact with bolts, i.e. Xerxes' bridge over the Hellespont, A.Pers.71

ὁδόω.definition: lead by the right way, A.Pr.813; ib.498: c. inf., who put mortals on the way to wisdom, Id.Ag.176 ; of things, direct, ordain, E.Ion1050 :—Pass., to be on the right way, Hdt.4.139

ὀδύνη.definition: pain of mind, grief, distress, once in Il., grief for him, 15.25: more freq. in Od., always in pl., 1.242; 2.79,al.: after Hom. the pl. was most common in both senses, S.Tr.959, 986 ; Ar.Ach.526; opp. Antipho Soph.49;…

ὄζαινα.definition: a fetid polypus in the nose; a strong-smelling sea-polypus, also called and Call.Fr.38

ὀζόομαι.definition: Pass., put forth branches or knots, Hp.Nat.Puer.22; Thphr.CP3.5.1

ὄζω.definition: Dor. Theoc.1.149 : impf; freq. impers., there is a smell from it as of violets, Hdt.3.23; there is a sweet smell from the skin, Ar.Pl.1020; Cratin.Jun.1; there seemed to be a most foul smell from . . , Lys.6.1; no sce…

ὀθόνη.definition: fine linen, in Hom. always pl., fine linen; later, sails, AP12.53.8 , cf. 10.5 : sg., sail-cloth, sail, Luc.JTr.46, VH2.37

οἴγω.definition: Hes.Op.819, etc.; later AP9.356 : fut. E.Cyc.502: aor. Il.24.457; but augm. forms usu. have in Ep. ; part. Il. : Ion. pf. Pass. Herod.4.55: the compd. or is much commoner, cf. also Il.6.89; ib.298; E.HF332; Id.Alc.547…

οἰδέω.definition: rarely Plu.2.734f: impf. Od.5.455; metaph., when affairs were in a ferment, Hdt.3.76, 127; metaph. from a boil or abscess, Pl.Grg.518e; Plu.Sol.19; also, of inflated style, Ar.Ra.940, cf. Plu.Cic.26

οἴδησις.definition: swelling, fermenting, Pl.Ti.70c; puffiness, Phld.Vit.p.27 J.; of dropsy, Hippiatr.38

ὀϊζύω.definition: aor. wail, mourn; c. acc. rei, suffer, 14.89: abs., to be miserable or suffer, Od.4.152, 23.307. of pres. short in Hom., long in A.R.4.1324, 1374; in aor. always long.]

οἴζω.definition: cry lament, A.D.Adv.128.10, who also coins to expl

οἰκέω.definition: Ep. Hes.Th.330, Locr; colonize, settle in, Th.1.8, cf. 2.27, etc.; prob. in E.Fr.360.11; i.e. to be deported, POxy.1101.24 : in pf. Pass., to be settled in, occupy, Hdt.1.27; ib.142

οἴκησις.definition: the act of dwelling or inhabiting; management, administration, Pl.Min.321b

οἰκητήρ.definition: poet. for S.OC627, restored by Herm. for in A.Th.19

οἰκίδιον.definition: Dim. of small house; tower on the back of an elephant, in pl., Plb.Fr.162B

οἰκιτιεύς.definition: Com. word for with play on Bion ap.Ath.4.162d

οἰκονόμος.definition: one who manages a household, =; generally, manager, administrator, opp. Id.Pol.1314b7, etc.: hence

οἰκόσιτος.definition: taking one's meals at home; living in a house, of a mouse, opp. Babr.108.4; cf

οἰκοσόος.definition: maintaining the house, of an economical wife, opp. Max.98: poet. Nonn.D.21.270

οἰκούρημα.definition: the watch or keeping of a house; keeping the house, staying at home, E.Heracl.700

οἰκουρία.definition: housekeeping and its cares, in pl; keeping-at-home, esp. of women, Plu.2.271e, Cor.35

οἰμάω.definition: only fut. and aor., swoop or pounce; abs., dart along, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.62

οἰμώζω.definition: Hom.Epigr.14.20, Tyrt.7, Ar.Ra.257, etc; in familiar Att., as a curse, plague take you ! Ar.Ach.1035; Id.Ra.257; Id.Pl.876; Id.Nu.217; Id.Pl.58, cf. Luc.Gall.23; Ar.Ra.178, cf. X.HG2.3.56, Men.Epit.428; Ar.Ach.840; Id…

οἰναρίζω.definition: strip off vine-leaves, as is done when the grapes are ripening, Ar.Pax1147, Phan.Hist.37

οἰνίδιον.definition: Dim. of small wine, poor wine, Apollod. ap. D.L.10.11

οἰνίζω.definition: resemble wine, Thphr. ap; Med., procure wine by barter, buy wine, . . Il.7.472; 8.506, cf. 546: in later Prose, Max.Tyr.39.1; Luc.VH1.9

οἰνοποτάζω.definition: drink wine, Il.20.84, Od.6.309, 20.262, Anacr.94.1, Phoc.11

οἰνόφυτος.definition: planted or grown with vines; Act., planting vines, Nonn.D.21.174

οἰνοχοεύω.definition: Od.21.142; part. 1.143; inf; c. acc., she was pouring out nectar, 4.3; . . . . Il.1.598: metaph., Plu.Per.7; Dionys.Eleg.4.1:—Pass., Plu.2.349f

οἰνόω.definition: intoxicate, Critias6.28D; Pass., turn into wine, Nonn.D.11.517

οἰοβώτας.definition: feeding alone, prop. of cattle, metaph. of Ajax, = S.Aj.614

οἰόζωνος.definition: alone and girt up, i.e. lonely wayfarer, S.OT846

οἴομαι.definition: in Hom. always uncontr. (exc; impersonal, only Od.19.312, there comes a boding into my heart

οἰόομαι.definition: Pass., to be left alone, forsaken, Ep. Verb, only in aor., Il.6.1, 11.401; Q.S.6.527

οἰοπέδη.definition: perh. a woollen bandage for sore feet, AP7.401

οἰοπολέω.definition: roam alone, E.Cyc.74 : c. acc. loci, roam over, of shepherds, AP7.657

οἰοχίτων.definition: with only a tunic on, lightly clad, Od.14.489, Nonn.D.8.16

ὀϊστεύω.definition: shoot arrows, whom; trans., shoot with an arrow, AP5.57 ; Nonn.D.15.322

οἴστρημα.definition: the smart of a gadfly's sting, metaph., S.OT1318; ravings of madness, AP6.51

οἰσύπη.definition: also the grease extracted from sheep's wool , Hdt.4.187; Hp.Mul.2.195; used for medicinal purposes, Dsc. and Plin. ll.cc.: —freq. confused with

οἰχνέω.definition: go, come, Il.5.790,15.640 (in Iterat; like to be gone, Id.Aj.564; Id.El.313

οἴχομαι.definition: impf. , the only; rarely in a general sense, go or come, without the idea of departure, and without a perfect sense, Il.1.53, cf. 5.495; more freq. go, go away, go off, Il.1.380, 13.38, 23.564, Od.17.104, al.: but usu…

ὀκέλλω.definition: trans. of seamen, run [a ship] aground or on shore, Hdt.l.c., Th.l.c.; of a wave, E.IT1379

ὄκλασις.definition: crouching with bent hams, squatting, Hp.Art.82, Luc.Salt.41

ὄκλασμα.definition: a Persian dance in which the dancer squatted from time to time, Ar.Fr.344b

ὀκνέω.definition: Ep. Il.5.255: impf. 20.155: fut; of shame or fear , I shrink from being called, fear to be called, S.Ph.93, cf. Th.5.61, Lys.Fr.23; shrink from naming, hesitate to name, D.2.19, cf. Pl.Grg.462e; . . D.18.103, cf. 24.7…

ὄκνος.definition: shrinking, hesitation; personified, as title of picture by Polygnotus, Paus.10.29.2, Plin.HN35.137, cf. D.S.1.97

ὀκριάομαι.definition: Pass., to be made rough or jagged: metaph., they grew furiously angry with each other, Od.18.33; enraged, Lyc.545

ὀκτάτονος.definition: eight-stretched, the eight arms of the octopus, AP9.14

ὀλεθριάω.definition: to be on the point of death, Archig. ap. Aët.9.40

ὀλέκω.definition: impf. without augm. Il.11.150; Iterat. 19.135:—pres. Phot., Suid.:—ruin, destroy, kill, Hom. always in last sense, and mostly of men, Il.18.172, cf. 15.249, Theoc.22.108, etc. ; but in Od.22.305, of birds which prey o…

ὀλιγαῦλαξ.definition: having but little arable land, AP6.226 Brunck)

ὀλιγόω.definition: lessen, diminish, LXXHb.3.12; ib.Pr.10.27; his soul was grieved, ib.Jd.10.16,al

ὀλιγωρία.definition: Ion. an esteeming lightly; neglect of duty, negligence, Decret. ap. D.18.74; Eun.Hist.p.257 D

ὀλίγωρος.definition: little-caring, lightly-esteeming; of things, scornful, . . Nicom.Com.1.2

ὁλίζω.definition: make into a single whole, Olymp.inPhd.p.86 N
